questions.question_text: The `refreshToken()` call is now awaited and its failure throws an `AuthError`. What would happen if this function is called from a non-async context, and how would you handle the resulting unhandled promise rejection?

criteria.name: identifies_promise_rejection
criteria.description: Recognizes that calling an async function without await leads to an unhandled promise rejection

criteria.name: proposes_error_boundary
criteria.description: Suggests wrapping the call in try-catch or using .catch() handler

questions.question_text: You introduced a new `SessionManager` class. Explain the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) trade-offs of having this class handle both session creation and session validation. Would you split it? Why or why not?

criteria.name: identifies_dual_responsibility
criteria.description: Identifies that creation and validation are separate concerns

criteria.name: argues_tradeoff
criteria.description: Makes a reasoned argument for or against splitting, with justification
